item.title: REVIEW: Tennessee Williams deep cut Summer and Smoke warms up Crow’s Theatre
item.description: I wondered if further following the directive to push upward instead of outward, balancing the corporeal dark with a little more spiritual lightness, might have made this ambitious and heartfelt production spark just a little bit hotter.

item.title: Review of MJ: The Musical among winners at the 2025 Nathan Cohen Awards
item.description: The Canadian Theatre Critics Association has announced the winners of the 2025 Nathan Cohen Awards for Excellence in Critical Writing. This year’s prizes for outstanding review and critical essay were adjudicated by Natasha Tripney, international editor of the Stage.

item.title: Copperbelt’s creative team crossed continents to do Natasha Mumba’s debut play justice
item.description: Zambian dialect coach Chiluba Katongo Nosfu worked with the cast, and also provided translation support for Mumba’s script: Copperbelt’s characters regularly interject words and phrases from Bemba — one of over 70 languages spoken in Zambia — into their English dialogue.

item.title: The Grand Theatre’s music-infused Piaf/Dietrich considers fame, friendship, and desire
item.description: “The extremes of both characters gives us a lot to consider and experience for how to live," says director Rachel Peake. "Should we lead with passion or precision? It’s sort of a no-brainer that happiness lies somewhere in the middle."

item.title: Q&A: Hybrid conference explores the potential of VR theatre in Canada
item.description: Single Thread Theatre’s Performance and Extended Realities Conference features a mix of live performances, interactive digital presentations, and technical deep dives, as well as virtual and in-person installations.

item.title: REVIEW: At The Theatre Centre, Searching for Aimai renders inheritance visible without offering resolution
item.description: Playwright-performer Coleen Shirin MacPherson refers to herself as “colonized upon arrival,” born in Canada yet shaped by migrations and erasures that predate her birth. “I don’t have an ancient song or a lullaby that connects us across generations,” she tells her child. That absence — of song, language, and unbroken tradition — propels the Cahoots Theatre production.

item.title: REVIEW: Eldritch’s Night at the Grand Guignol features spurting blood and severed eyes
item.description: The show hits the pulpy B-movie bullseye at which the indie company has long taken aim. Over the course of four playlets, a catalogue of deaths unfurls — shlockily! gorily! — in macabre locales.

item.title: Spotlight: Ma-Anne Dionisio
item.description: “Art has a very significant healing aspect to it,” says Ma-Anne Dionisio. “The performance aspect, for me, always comes secondary.”

item.title: ‘You have to be humble about what you don’t know’: Pamela Mala Sinha reflects on the moment she became a writer (part two)
item.description: Over the course of 90 minutes, Pamela and I spoke about her trajectory from actor to first-time playwright with Crash, the frustrations and anxieties of being a working artist, and the way her family has consistently inspired both her creative and personal lives.

item.title: REVIEW: In the Maritimes, The Heterosexuals unpacks the traps of heteronormativity
item.description: Watching Johnnie McNamara Walker make a space for himself with a Fredericton audience was captivating. As a performer, he’s wickedly charismatic. He talks with his hands, asks with his brow, and paces to keep up with his frenetic writing and delivery.
